principle: A bound asset, source marker, or technically present feature is not a completed quality improvement until a player-facing runtime delta is observable and the responsible system passes regression.

surfaces.goal: Readable locomotion, acting, attack, hit and recovery with weight, timing and secondary motion.
Clear hierarchy, safe-area layout, touchable controls, consistent visual language and state feedback.
Fast inspect/equip/unequip/compare/use flow with authoritative equipped state and unmistakable selection feedback.

surfaces.appliesWhen: audio is allowed by owner/game intent
surfaces.goal: State-adaptive music, readable mix, spatial ambience and event-synced feedback without masking gameplay.
Effects strengthen impact and telegraph readability without hiding threats or controls.
Responsive framing, bounded impact response and readable threat/interaction space.
Region identity, depth, material separation and gameplay readability through native lighting/material systems.
Distinct routes, landmarks, props and encounter/resource rhythm instead of empty expansion.
Every important input has immediate, spatially or contextually anchored acknowledgement and result feedback.
First-play controls, current goal and next action are visible when needed without blocking play.
Readable text, reduced-motion/volume controls where relevant and no inaccessible critical-only cue.
Touch-first controls, safe areas, no overlap, reliable pointer lifecycle and context-sized actions.
Stable frame pacing and bounded presentation cost while keeping high-value feedback.
Presentation/UI build-up never corrupts or obscures save, restore, reconnect or retry meaning.
Remote players/actions/state changes are legible without client-authority drift.

surfaces.appliesWhen: new or revised content is added
surfaces.goal: New content connects to existing world, progression, rewards and presentation language instead of isolated quantity.
Anticipation, action, impact, recoil/recovery and response timing are clearly felt while gameplay authority stays unchanged.
Characters, enemies, equipment, environment and UI share an intentional game-specific visual language.

requirements: DOM/canvas/WebGL presentation must be driven by real gameplay state rather than demo-only animation.
Motion must be perceptible at normal play scale; tiny whole-sprite bob/rotation alone cannot close a motion gap when articulated or layered motion is feasible.
Inventory and menus must be touch-usable, scroll-safe and persist authoritative state.
WebAudio/HTMLAudio build-up must respect owner mute/SFX intent and prove state transitions instead of merely loading an audio file.
Responsive mobile capture and actual input replay are required.
Use Animator/AnimationClip/BlendTree or equivalent native rig motion when actors are articulated.
Use Canvas/uGUI or UI Toolkit with authoritative inventory/equipment state and mobile input.
Use AudioMixer/state transitions/spatial audio where applicable and preserve user volume/mute behavior.
Use native lighting/material/post-processing within mobile performance budgets.
Unity WebGL and app must share canonical Unity gameplay/UI source rather than diverging clones.

Articulated PLAYER/HUMANOID_NPC/CREATURE motion must use real joints/rig animation: Animator/AnimationTrack, Motor6D/Bone transforms or equivalent native articulation. Root-only CFrame movement, whole-model bobbing, or weld-only mannequins cannot close motion quality.
Locomotion must cover idle/walk/jog/run plus start/stop/turn; applicable actors also cover jump/land, attack/skill, hit and death with cross-fade/blend and playback-speed synchronization.
Secondary/procedural motion should add torso/weapon/appendage follow-through; IKControl or grounded correction is preferred when it materially improves contact/readability.

Roblox UI must be touch-first, safe-area aware, state-driven, and verify menu/back/scroll/modal behavior in Studio. Inventory/equipment must show authoritative equipped state and preserve it through save/rejoin when persistent.

Roblox audio requires SoundService/SoundGroup-oriented mix discipline where applicable: separate music/SFX/UI/ambience intent, state-adaptive BGM transitions, bounded ducking, positional sound for world sources, and no re-enabling effects the owner intentionally disabled.
VFX/particles/highlights/beams must be event-bound and telegraph-safe; camera shake/FOV/lighting effects are presentation-only and bounded on mobile.
Lighting/Atmosphere/ColorCorrection/Bloom/material changes must improve scene readability and region identity without hiding hazards or exceeding mobile budget.
A Roblox quality PASS requires actual Studio input plus captured runtime evidence. Static source markers, semantic asset atoms, or successful binding alone cannot prove perceptible quality.
For every high-value player-facing surface changed, Studio replay must demonstrate the visible/audible state transition and the relevant regression path.

priorityPolicy.rule: When the same game has WEB, ROBLOX and UNITY build-up work, share the game goal and acceptance intent, but let each platform use native implementation. Roblox receives the strictest motion/audio/UI runtime evidence because superficial binding is a recurring quality risk.
